knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Section 9: bathers are the biggest source of nitrogen compounds, arriving in sweat and urine.
Section 9.5: urea needs a breakdown step before it can bind chlorine, which can mean a wait of three or four hours, whereas ammonia reacts within minutes.
Section 9.5: effective disinfection requires organic nitrogen to be controlled, achieved by maintaining breakpoint chlorination at all times.

practicalCriteria: For a supplied busy-day scenario, sets a testing frequency and records the bather load and weather.
Removes supplied debris from the water surface before opening and records the removal.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Bather load and test record for the assessed day
stopWorkCriteria: Free chlorine below minimum during a busy period: close or restrict the pool as the operator directs and escalate.
Body fluid spill in the pool: follow the response in pool-cleaning-L09 and stop work until the area is safe.
